script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. NEW YORK CITY - DAY

A bustling city street. CARS HONK, PEOPLE TALK, SUN SHINES.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

MRS. JENKINS (60s, kindly) pours COFFEE for MR. GARCIA (40s, tired), who sits at the counter.

MRS. JENKINS
(looking at Mr. Garcia)
You look tired.

MR. GARCIA
(smiling wearily)
Another late night at the hospital.

INT. HOSPITAL LOBBY - DAY

MR. GARCIA, a NURSE, and DR. SIMMONS (30s, intense) argue over a patient. DR. SIMMONS storms off.

EXT. PARK - DAY

Mr. Garcia sits on a bench, defeated. A YOUNG GIRL, MIA (12), rides by on her bike. She asks if he's okay.

MIA
(pointing to her dog)
My dog, Max, needs a friend. He's lonely.

INT. MR. GARCIA'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Mr. Garcia brings Mia and Max inside. They share stories, laughs, and a meal.

INT. DR. SIMMONS' APARTMENT - NIGHT

Dr. Simmons throws books and papers across the room in frustration. Her phone rings. It's Mr. Garcia.

DR. SIMMONS
(yelling)
I can't do this anymore!

MR. GARCIA
(calmly)
I understand. I've felt the same way.

DR. SIMMONS
(pausing)
What changed?

MR. GARCIA
(sighs)
Mia.

INT. MR. GARCIA'S APARTMENT - DAY

Mr. Garcia and Mia work in the garden. He teaches her about the importance of growing things.

INT. HOSPITAL WAITING ROOM - DAY

Mr. Garcia sees Dr. Simmons, looking defeated and sad. He approaches her.

MR. GARCIA
You quit?

DR. SIMMONS
Yes.

MR. GARCIA
Why?

DR. SIMMONS
(tearfully)
Because I didn't think I was making a difference.

MR. GARCIA
(smiling)
Come see Mia and me. You can make a difference in her life.

INT. MR. GARCIA'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Dr. Simmons arrives, smiling. She meets Mia and Max.

INT. PARK - DAY

Mr. Garcia, Mia, and Dr. Simmons sit on a bench, watching children play.

DR. SIMMONS
(smiling)
This feels right.

MR. GARCIA
Second chances are rare, but they're worth it.

FADE OUT.
